subject.title: fix(context-engine): bound deferred turn maintenance with a per-task timeout (AI-assisted)

question: Should core permanently expose this new opt-in maintenance-timeout and synchronous queue-fence contract, or should deferred maintenance reuse an existing timeout/abort contract instead?
rationale: Source review can establish that the implementation is coherent, but it cannot choose the enduring public configuration and plugin-abandonment policy; that decision affects config growth, queue API ownership, and what guarantees external context engines receive.

options.title: Approve the opt-in contract
options.body: Keep the dedicated disabled-by-default timeout and synchronous host-side fence, document plugin-private side-effect limits, then require exact-head green validation before merge.

options.title: Reuse an existing timeout
options.body: Refactor maintenance onto the existing compaction safety budget or abort machinery, accepting that upgrade behavior and legitimate long-running maintenance need separate compatibility proof.

options.title: Define cancellation first
options.body: Pause this PR and design an explicit context-engine cancellation or abandonment API before landing any timeout behavior.

recommendation.title: Approve the opt-in contract
recommendation.body: Keep the dedicated disabled-by-default timeout and synchronous host-side fence, document plugin-private side-effect limits, then require exact-head green validation before merge.

likelyOwner.reason: The context-engine architecture provenance makes this person the best available owner for its permanent host/plugin lifecycle contract.
